Chela James.

Senior Bioinformatician/Data Scientist at Human Technopole

ORCID in LinkedIn

01 / Work

Career development

  • From molecular biology to bioinformatics

    It started with molecular neurobiology using the model organism C.elegans looking for novel neurotransmitter transporter proteins. Working with this organism I developed an interest in developmental biology and went on to study the formation of teeth, I continued the theme of developmental biology looking at early heart development. It was during my next role I discovered bioinformatics, my supervisor handed me a external hard disk drive with exome sequencing data and asked me to deal with it. I spent the next few months converting my desktop PC to linux, learning the command line and the myriad tools required to align sequence data, call variants and annotate them.

  • Data analyses

    As a bioinformatician my guiding principal is understanding the science and having the flexibility to attempt new methods and present data in clear and interesting ways. One example of this is my collaboration with Emanuele Azzoni and Marella de Bruijn in this paper: onset of circulation triggers a metabolic switch required for endothelial to hematopoietic transition. I processed the single-cell transcriptomic data and presented it in a useable format

  • Data handling

    As well as data analyses I am charged with processing hundreds of samples so I developed a pipeline to process the data from raw sequencing reads to processed data. The files are stored in a logical structure and a database is used to track the samples, their metadata and the processing status. For this I developed a simple json schema which is easy to access and update.

  • AI and agentic programming

    Artificial intelligence has offered a myriad of new methods of working and I am very curious about exploiting it to improve our analyses. One example I am pursuing is in quality control. I routinely process thousands of samples and on the whole they pass QC. Using agentic AI I have created a script that surveys a multiqc output and picks out the outliers, only the selected outliers are submitted to the seqera or openai agents to speculate about the reasons why they may have failed.

02 / Milestones

Achievements

  • 1999

    My PhD Project

    This was a speculative project searching for a novel protein that may not have existed. I used diverse techniques including molecular biology techniques including southern blotting and microinjection of constructs into the model organism C.elegans.

  • 2002

    First PostDoc

    I published Tooth development is independent of a Hox patterning programme This work was very interesting on the level of developmental biology and the role of the Hox genes and also technically challenging.

  • 2011

    Switch to bioinformatics

    Having been given sequencing data to deal with, I went through an intensive period of self teaching in-order to understand the data and the tools required to process it.

  • 2021

    Cancer data analysis

    Having joined the Sottoriva lab, I introduced the nextflow pipeline system to their data processing and analysis.

  • 2026

    National Facilities

    The Human Technopole National Facility for Data Handling and Analysis (NF-DHA) is a new facility that will provide the Italian scientific community with access to high-performance computing resources and expertise in data analysis. I am leading the development of the bioinformatics pipelines and data analysis workflows for the facility, which will support a wide range of research projects in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and other omics fields.

03 / hobbies

Outside work

  • Languages

    I have a passion for languages and have studied several over the years. I achieved a B2/C1 level in in Italian, and have a good command of Spanish. I enjoy learning new languages and exploring different cultures through language.
